# Canonical continuation of the analytics build

The implementation run is explicitly paused at 73 accepted tasks. This replaces the previous validation-only restart with an actual canonical planning migration. Retained execution and failure history remain historical evidence; they are not newly manufactured version-2 acceptance receipts.

## Revised boundaries

The remaining work is represented in `canonical-plan.json`, with an independent review required before compilation/migration. Nine additional splits separate finalization from check invalidation; extension lifecycle from exposure integration; locked predictive classification from Question persistence and report honesty; authorization types from Decision validation; use lifecycle tests from command registration; inspection-look hooks from recurrence fault fixtures; evaluation separation/audit tests from cohort metric tests; and retention apply from interrupted-cleanup recovery.

There are 201 graph nodes, including 73 retained completed records and 128 unfinished units. All 284 checklist entries have exactly one executable owner. Every original FR, SC and ordered edge is retained verbatim: 234 functional requirements, 219 success criteria and 115 edge cases, totaling 568 original obligations. The 769-criterion registry combines those final obligations with each node's assigned local boundary.

## Dependencies and acceptance

Inputs select registered producers and exact capabilities. Named export contracts remain explicitly weaker than behavioral boundary checks. Missing or ambiguous producer selection prevents compilation. Completed producer availability does not grant permission to invent missing behavior. Scope and source ownership are separate from ordering; shared writes/resources are governed by admission.

Local acceptance tests the assigned boundary. Whole-feature requirements remain attached to named final verification after their contributors. The 007 corrective successor now owns verification after the join/measurement correction rather than assigning new contributor obligations to its already completed historical predecessor.

The complete original release/CLI/browser/live-worker checks remain in the original feature and convergence units. Scoped checks cannot replace those obligations. The accepted model ladder remains Luna xhigh, Sol 6.1 medium, Sol 6.1 xhigh; no Astra is introduced.

## Migration and safeguards

`dag plan migrate` explicitly imports this validated and independently approved manifest into the same stopped run. Existing completed task objects, task IDs, run ID, exact completed dependencies, attempts/cycle budgets, results and salvage refs are retained. Historical task and contract digests protect those imports. Pending definitions are produced by the canonical compiler. The migration journal stores the complete prior run and blocks dispatch after interrupted writes.

The reliability envelope is version 2 and embeds the same manifest. It contains no separately authored tasks table or work-command override. The project adapter derives its compatibility view from that manifest. Workers and reviewers receive local/deferred acceptance and can emit grounded planning findings. Repeated planning failures hold the consumer before exhausting its remaining model budget; graph correction remains explicit.

The controller's incidents, semantic/infrastructure counts and attempts remain in the same ledger. The persistent operator pause survives migration/amendment, and dispatch requires an explicit continuation. Retained worktrees and earlier failed source are unverified candidates; only current owned changes may be reused after comparison with current HEAD and fresh acceptance.

## Verification limits

Deterministic planning validation establishes registry coverage and declared graph consistency. It does not prove all prose prerequisites, method correctness or model capability. Independent semantic review is therefore mandatory. Migration/graph validation is not successful product implementation. Sustained acceptance and recurrence of missing-prerequisite failures must be evaluated during the subsequent live run.

The current control-project specs are the authority: ten integration copies had drifted to older wording. Current text was restored before semantic review; the registry also includes the two obligations missing from those older copies.

## Review and validation outcome

Independent Luna xhigh review approved canonical revision `ebfebd8ebcd873bf29ab2aa675985835115c88a980fe2c69fc165e8e488f3670` with no remaining findings after two bounded correction reviews. All 25 feature/task plans validate, the structural audit resolves 234 FRs and 115 edges, and the controller/migration regression suites passed 36 tests. The updated review-reference regression and TypeScript compilation also pass.

Active release, acceptance and handoff denominators are 234 FR, 219 SC and 115 EC, plus 61 T cases and eight paths: 637 final matrix rows. Historical verification and dependency-replan snapshots retain their earlier counts as historical evidence. Original product tests and policy thresholds were preserved.
